title: Purpose of Publication
content: The publication of OC4IDS data aligns with the Open Contracting principles of transparency and accountability in public infrastructure projects. By making this information accessible, we aim to foster trust, efficiency, and innovation in the procurement and implementation of infrastructure projects.

subsections.title: Uses of the Data
subsections.content: The National Infrastructure Disclosure Platform data empowers various stakeholders: government agencies can improve project management and resource allocation; civil society organizations can monitor project progress and impacts; businesses can identify opportunities and enhance competitiveness; and citizens can engage in informed discussions about public infrastructure investments. Specific use cases include budget monitoring, performance analysis, and environmental impact assessments.

title: Publication Details
content: We are committed to providing high-quality, timely, and comprehensive data in line with Open Contracting for Infrastructure Data Standards (OC4IDS).

subsections.title: Creation of OC4IDS Datasets
subsections.content: Our data undergoes rigorous quality checks during the nightly refresh process. We ensure data completeness, accuracy, and compliance with the OC4IDS schema before publication. Data is collected from various government systems, including procurement platforms, project management tools, and financial systems. It is then processed, transformed into the OC4IDS format, and validated against the schema.

subsections.title: Project Identifier Generation
subsections.content: Our project identifier system ensures unique identification of each infrastructure project, facilitating data linking and tracking throughout the project lifecycle. This supports the Open Contracting principle of data accessibility and usability. Each identifier is generated using the project's unique identifier from our internal systems, prefixed with 'OC4IDS-[COUNTRY_CODE]-', ensuring no conflicts or duplications across different publishing entities.

subsections.title: Accessing the Data
subsections.content: We provide multiple data access options to cater to different user needs and technical capabilities, adhering to the Open Contracting principle of making data open by default. Data can be accessed via our data portal at https://infrastructure.opendata.gov, RESTful API, and bulk downloads in various formats including JSON and CSV. Our API documentation is available at https://infrastructure.opendata.gov/api-docs.

subsections.title: Linked Datasets
subsections.content: Our OC4IDS data is linked to other relevant datasets, including the national company registry and geographical information system. These linkages are made using standard identifiers, enhancing the richness and usability of the data.

title: Scope and Format
content: Our publication scope is designed to provide a comprehensive view of public infrastructure projects, supporting informed decision-making and public oversight.

subsections.title: Inclusions and Exclusions
subsections.content: Included: All major public infrastructure projects from 2018 onwards, across all government levels, with a total value exceeding $1 million. This covers sectors such as transportation, energy, water and sanitation, and public buildings. Excluded: Projects involving national security, sensitive data, or below the $1 million threshold.

subsections.title: Data Formats
subsections.content: Data is available via our data portal at https://infrastructure.opendata.gov, RESTful API, and bulk downloads in various formats including JSON and CSV. Our API documentation is available at https://infrastructure.opendata.gov/api-docs.

title: Data Reuse
content: Our choice of the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license reflects our commitment to the Open Contracting principle of open data.

subsections.title: Terms of Use
subsections.content: Under the CC BY 4.0 license, you are free to share (copy and redistribute the material in any medium or format) and adapt (remix, transform, and build upon the material) for any purpose, even commercially. The licensor cannot revoke these freedoms as long as you follow the license terms. For more details, visit https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/.

title: Data Quality Assurance
content: We are committed to maintaining high data quality standards in our OC4IDS publication.

subsections.title: Data Validation Process
subsections.content: Our rigorous validation process ensures that all published data adheres to the OC4IDS schema and meets our quality benchmarks. This involves automated checks using the OC4IDS Data Review Tool, as well as manual reviews by our data quality team to identify and rectify any discrepancies.

subsections.title: Error Handling and Corrections
subsections.content: We have a robust system for identifying and correcting errors in published data, ensuring the integrity and reliability of our OC4IDS datasets. Users can report errors via our feedback form at https://infrastructure.opendata.gov/feedback. Corrections are tracked and documented in our change history, which is publicly accessible.

title: Data Retention and Archiving
content: Our data retention policy ensures long-term accessibility and historical analysis of infrastructure project data.

subsections.title: Archiving Strategy
subsections.content: We maintain comprehensive archives of all published OC4IDS data, allowing for historical analysis and long-term transparency. Archived data is stored securely in our data warehouse and is accessible for retrospective analysis. We guarantee data retention for a minimum of 10 years after project completion.

subsections.title: Data Updates and Versioning
subsections.content: Our versioning system allows users to track changes and updates to project data over time, maintaining a clear audit trail. Each update is documented with details of changes made and their impact on the data. We use semantic versioning (e.g., v1.0.0) for major releases and provide a changelog at https://infrastructure.opendata.gov/changelog.

title: Contact Information
content: In line with Open Contracting principles of participation and collaboration, we welcome feedback and engagement from all stakeholders.

subsections.title: How to Reach Us
subsections.content: For inquiries or feedback, please contact our Open Data Team at opendata@publicworks.gov. For technical support, reach out to techsupport@publicworks.gov. Our physical address is 123 Government Street, Capital City.

subsections.title: Feedback Mechanism
subsections.content: We value your input. You can provide feedback through our online form at https://infrastructure.opendata.gov/feedback or during our quarterly stakeholder meetings. All feedback is reviewed and considered for future improvements to our data publication process.

title: License
content: Our choice of the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license reflects our commitment to the Open Contracting principle of open data. This license ensures that our data can be freely used, modified, and shared by all, maximizing its potential impact.

The licensor cannot revoke these freedoms as long as you follow the license terms. For more details, visit https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/.

title: Future Development Plans
content: We are dedicated to expanding and improving our OC4IDS publication. Our plans include increasing historical data coverage, enhancing data quality, and developing user-friendly tools for data analysis and visualization.

subsections.title: Roadmap
subsections.content: Q3 2024: Implement geospatial data extensions for all infrastructure projects. Q4 2024: Launch an interactive data visualization tool. Q1 2025: Extend historical data coverage to projects from 2015 onwards. Q2 2025: Integrate machine learning algorithms for data quality checks and anomaly detection.

subsections.title: Stakeholder Engagement
subsections.content: We conduct annual surveys and quarterly focus groups to gather input from data users. This feedback directly informs our development priorities. To participate, sign up at https://infrastructure.opendata.gov/engage.

title: Disclaimer
content: Access to our data portal does not imply verification of the accuracy, completeness, or timeliness of the information provided. The data is collected from various sources and may contain inaccuracies. The Department of Public Works and Infrastructure is not responsible for decisions made based on this data. Users are encouraged to cross-reference critical information and to report any discrepancies they may find.

title: Additional Documentation
content: For further information, users can refer to our comprehensive documentation suite.

subsections.title: Available Resources
subsections.content: Technical Documentation: https://infrastructure.opendata.gov/docs, API Guide: https://infrastructure.opendata.gov/api-guide, Data Schema: https://infrastructure.opendata.gov/schema, User Guides: https://infrastructure.opendata.gov/user-guides, FAQ: https://infrastructure.opendata.gov/faq

title: Extensions and Modifications
content: To meet specific national requirements and enhance data usability, we have implemented several extensions to the core OC4IDS schema.

subsections.title: Custom Extensions
subsections.content: Environmental Impact: Adds fields for environmental assessments and mitigation measures. Social Impact: Includes data on community engagement and benefit-sharing mechanisms. Project Milestones: Provides more granular tracking of project progress. The full documentation for these extensions is available at https://infrastructure.opendata.gov/extensions.

subsections.title: Codelists
subsections.content: We use standard OC4IDS codelists where applicable. For country-specific needs, we have extended certain codelists, such as the project sector and subsector classifications. Our custom codelists are documented at https://infrastructure.opendata.gov/codelists.
